extracted.intended_audience: applicants for registration to practice before the USPTO (patent bar applicants), OED staff, and USPTO decisionmakers
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and legal/regulatory criteria used by the USPTO (OED and Director) to evaluate whether an applicant possesses the scientific and technical qualifications to sit for the patent registration exam and when (if ever) regulatory requirements may be waived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory standard — necessary qualifications to render valuable service
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(A), the Director may require proof that practitioners are 'possessed of the necessary qualifications to render applicants or other persons valuable service, advice, and assistance in the presentation or prosecution of their applications or other business before the Office.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statutory standard is the primary responsibility for protecting the public from unqualified practitioners and frames all regulatory and Bulletin requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satisfactory proof of scientific and technical qualifications (37 C.F.R. § 11.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants for the registration examination must provide 'satisfactory proof of their scientific and technical qualifications' sufficient to enable them to render patent applicants valuable service (cited to 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.7(a)(2)(ii) and (b)(1)(i)(C)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meeting this proof requirement is distinct from merely taking the exam — applicants must demonstrate substantive technical competence in science/engineering through the means described in the Bulletin or by equivalent evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bulletin Section III — Category A: Bachelor's degree in listed technical subject
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Category A, an applicant must have a Bachelor's degree in one of the recognized technical subjects listed in Section III of the General Requirements Bulletin (the Bulletin).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an applicant has a qualifying Category A degree, that typically establishes the required scientific/technical training. The Bulletin lists specific subjects (32 subjects referenced in the decision).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bulletin Section III — Category B: Bachelor's in other subject plus equivalent scientific/technical training
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Category B, an applicant with a Bachelor's degree in a subject not listed in Category A may qualify if he or she also has scientific and technical training 'equivalent to that of a Bachelor's degree in a subject listed in Category A.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category B contains subsections (i)-(iv) describing ways to establish equivalence and also allows case-by-case consideration of other education and life experience (see subsections (xii) and (xiii)). Applicants must submit objective evidence showing equivalence (e.g., coursework credit, documented training).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bulletin Section III — Category C: Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) test
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Category C, eligibility requires satisfying the specified degree criteria and successful completion (passing) of the Fundamentals of Engineering test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passing the FE is an alternate pathway to demonstrate technical competency when degree subjects differ from Category A list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case-by-case consideration / life experience (Bulletin B (xii) & (xiii))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bulletin permits consideration of 'other factors and other education, such as life experience, on a case-by-case basis with respect to scientific and technical training' to determine equivalence to a Category A Bachelor's degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such life-experience evidence must be objective and demonstrably equivalent to academic training; unsupported assertions or generalized descriptions of experience are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof on the applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants 'bear the burden of showing the requisite scientific and technical training' to qualify for the exam (Bulletin at 4 and decision text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant must produce objective evidence (transcripts, accredited credit, certificates, licensure, test results) rather than mere assertions; failure to present such evidence supports denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: High burden for applicants without a technical degree
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants without a technical degree have a 'high burden to show sufficient expertise and professionalism in science and/or engineering' (citing Premysler v. Lehman).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director assesses all evidence closely; anecdotal or conclusory claims of competence are unlikely to meet this high burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent review by USPTO Director when categories not met
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant does not qualify under Categories A, B, or C, the USPTO Director may conduct an independent review of the applicant's experience to determine compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.7(a)(2)(ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director exercises discretion in evaluating whether nontraditional credentials or experience equate to the requisite scientific/technical training (Premysler precedent cited).

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver standard for regulatory requirements (37 C.F.R. § 11.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-statutory regulatory requirements may be suspended or waived by the Director 'in an extraordinary situation, when justice requires' (37 C.F.R. § 11.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To succeed on a waiver request, an applicant must show an extraordinary situation warranting relief; failing to meet normal qualification standards generally will not suffice.

rubrics_metrics.name: No new evidence on petition for review (37 C.F.R. § 11.2(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: When petitioning the USPTO Director for review of an OED Director decision, 'the USPTO Director will consider no new evidence' (37 C.F.R. § 11.2(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should ensure the administrative record before OED is complete because additional documentation submitted only at the PFR stage will not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition/expected scope of 'valuable service'
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision explains that 'valuable service' encompasses a level of expertise enabling a practitioner to prepare and prosecute patent applications and draft specifications or claims of patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation focuses on whether the applicant can independently perform substantive patent-practice tasks that require scientific/technical knowledge, not merely ancillary tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective evidence requirement — conclusory letters insufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters of support (e.g., from a registered practitioner) must provide objective evidence of the applicant's scientific/technical training; conclusory endorsements without factual support are insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A supporting practitioner's opinion should be backed by specifics about the applicant's technical training/experience and, if making comparative statements, include the practitioner's own qualifications or the basis for comparison; otherwise the letter 'provides no objective evidence.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art searching alone is insufficient to qualify
rubrics_metrics.description: Longstanding precedent holds that 'mere patent searching' experience, by itself, is insufficient to demonstrate the scientific and technical qualifications required to sit for the examination (citing Gage v. Nadd and case law).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claiming technical competence based on patent searching, the applicant must show how such searching produced technical knowledge or training equivalent to formal coursework or licensure (with objective documentation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Must demonstrate ability to technically analyze prior art like a scientist/engineer
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant must provide objective evidence that he or she is 'actually capable of technically analyzing a prior art reference in the same way as a scientist or engineer.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General assertions that one 'analyzes claims' or 'routinely interprets patent claims' do not establish scientific/technical training absent demonstrative evidence (work product, credentials, evaluations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Core-competency and technology specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant should have 'core competencies within well defined and clearly identified technologies' rather than only experience searching across multiple unrelated technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrated depth in a defined technical area is more persuasive than breadth across disparate fields; evidence should identify technologies and the substantive technical tasks performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED staff initial evaluation and reviewable process
rubrics_metrics.description: OED staff members initially evaluate registration applications; their decisions are reviewable by the OED Director (37 C.F.R. § 11.2(c)), and the Director's final decision may be petitioned to the USPTO Director (37 C.F.R. § 11.2(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand the multi-tiered administrative process and timing/deadlines for submitting supporting evidence and appeals; substantive evidence must be in the record to be considered on review.
